Dear Buffalo Bills and Josh Allen,
I actually really liked your team a lot, and was a fan of Josh Allen, but I need to speak up regarding a commercial that made me wonder which decade I was in, where Mr. Allen appeared to make fun of those of us with Tourettes syndrome, which…believe it or not…are stacked with dope people that win grammy’s (Billy Eilish), become the goalie for the U.S. national team and Manchester United (Tim Howard), win the world series (Jim Eisrenrich) and people like me that support our communities (I cannot tell you how fucking tired I am of having to say this shit). As a middle-aged man, I am a seasoned recipient of jokes regarding my condition, however my instant reaction to what I perceive as someone mocking the symptoms I used to have (Coprolalia, what ya’ll call Tourette’s) is the same— disillusionment, sadness, rage, and an instant need to stand up for the little ones that look up to Mr. Allen. 

Regardless of whether or not Josh Allen understood what his Pizza Hut commercial meant (he did), it presents as him being unable to control himself, appearing to have Tourette's Syndrome while saying, “hut hut, hut hut hut, hut hut”, and then clinching the insult by saying, "I can't not do it". It’s not something that, as a grown man, I instantly perceive as targeted malice (it's definitely targeted). However, a little kid wearing a Josh Allen jersey, sitting on his couch with his family who are trying to support him during his journey through this neurological disorder, will not be able to process why his hero is making fun of him. 

He will feel all of the feelings that I have, combined with all of the constant torment and teasing that he endures on a daily basis, without the words to express himself. I’m not going to go on my soapbox and talk about how coprolalia isn’t Tourette syndrome, or discuss how most of 99% of us don’t have this symptom, or that most of us “grow out of it” (it’s called puberty, for some reason many of us lose the coprolalia symptom during it), but I am going to encourage you to be more conscientious about the potential impacts of your side hustles. 
What probably seemed like a goofy commercial to Mr. Allen (I don't actually think that, he knows what he was doing) is going to crush so many little kids who look up to him, and they’re going to wonder why he is making fun. They’re children, and even as an adult, it made me want to jump through the screen and make his “hut hut hut hut hut” shit last for a year, so he’d understand what it’s actually like. Our kids deserve better, and in no way, shape or form am I accusing Mr. Allen of anything (Ok, I am, but ya'll don't learn unless you're coddled), but I am encouraging all of you to be smarter about your impact.
